solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Alarm spread at a work place of Trump

indicators.note: letters spread about are scattered into a new order

parts.note: a machine that goes is working

explanation.surface: Panic breaks out at the office, which turns out to be Trump's own.
explanation.walkthrough: Mar-a-Lago is Trump's Florida resort and home, where he also conducts business.
explanation.definitionFit: Mar-a-Lago is Trump's private club and residence in Palm Beach, Florida.

clue.text: To piss, start to loosen skin

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A crude instruction pairing a toilet break with peeling something off.
explanation.walkthrough: Skin is a verb here: to peel an orange is to skin it.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin is a verb here, a plain synonym for stripping the outer layer off fruit.

clue.text: William's character: an arse

definitions.meaning: a weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, turned into an ass
arse is British slang for backside

explanation.surface: A put-down: someone called William is, by nature, an arse.
explanation.walkthrough: William is Shakespeare; his weaver Nick Bottom gets an ass's head, which makes the pairing with arse a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottom is a Shakespeare character and also a word for the backside.

clue.text: Order one to have new union

parts.note: a junction is where things join

explanation.surface: An instruction for someone to join a new trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: Union reads like a trade union but is used in its sense of a joining point.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the legal sense: a court's formal order to do or stop doing something.

clue.text: (& 26dn.) "Hell, me income's dodgy!" — absent peer

indicators.note: something dodgy is not right, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: HELL ME INCOME rearranged, ignoring the 's

explanation.surface: An exclamation from someone admitting their earnings are suspect, followed by a note that a member of the Lords is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Baroness Michelle Mone took leave of absence from the House of Lords amid the scandal over PPE contracts, so the quoted words are a joke about her money.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelle Mone is a Conservative member of the House of Lords who took a leave of absence in 2022.

clue.text: Buzz off darling — butt out

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong, so the letters are put in a new order
the butt is the end, and it goes out of the word

parts.note: DARLING with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone tells a sweetheart to go away and stop interfering.
explanation.walkthrough: Buzz off reads as a dismissal, but Buzz is the definition, and off is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Buzz Aldrin was the second man to walk on the Moon.

clue.text: Bad Count Dracula started admitting the French

indicators.note: the part of Dracula that starts it is its first letter

parts.note: to count up is to add

indicators.note: letting something in means holding it inside

explanation.surface: A villainous vampire count lets some French people in.
explanation.walkthrough: Count Dracula looks like one name, but Count is a verb and Dracula only supplies its initial; LE sits inside ADD-D.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad is meant in the sense of rotten, as an egg goes off; muddled is the other common sense.

clue.text: "Not a clue Brown" about to retire

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A nickname for Gordon Brown, the clueless prime minister, as he is about to step down.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was British prime minister from 2007 to 2010; here Brown is just a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunno is casual speech for I don't know, meaning not a clue.

clue.text: see 23dn.
Well outside measure by Sun editor

indicators.note: the first word goes outside the rest, holding it

parts.note: Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like Well!
an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: Something lies beyond the reach of a Sun newspaper editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is a British exclamation of surprise; it wraps around EN plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: A censor edits material by cutting what is not allowed.

clue.text: Abolition yearbook intended to get rid of AA

indicators.note: getting rid of letters removes them

parts.note: ANNUAL, a yearly book, without one A
two A's, one taken out of each word

explanation.surface: A plan to scrap a yearbook in order to shake off the motoring organisation AA.
explanation.walkthrough: AA is two separate A's, one taken from each word; the AA is a British motoring association, which the surface pretends is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulment abolishes something, as a law or marriage is declared void.

clue.text: Penny off Drug dealer's Guide!

indicators.note: the penny comes off the word

explanation.surface: A price reduction on a drug dealer's handbook.
explanation.walkthrough: Guide looks like a book title but is the verb or noun for someone showing people the way; the 's joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher guides people to their seats.

clue.text: Keen to conceal opposition leader's dodge

indicators.note: something concealed is hidden inside
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A politician eager to hide the Opposition leader's evasive trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Opposition leader reads as a politician, but it is just the first letter of opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to evade or keep clear of something.

clue.text: Trump's not much bothered about this US seed crop distribution

definitions.text: Trump's not much bothered about this

indicators.note: the letters are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: Trump is indifferent to how American seed harvests are shared out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a jibe: due process is the legal fairness Trump has been accused of brushing aside, and this points at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Due process is the principle of fair legal procedure, which the setter says Trump ignores.

clue.text: House, shitty location — a break for writers

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
the colon is the part of the gut where faeces form

explanation.surface: A grim house in a grim spot advertised as a writers' retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a British semi-detached house; a break for writers sounds like a retreat but is a punctuation pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicolon marks a pause in a sentence, a break in writing.

clue.text: Patronising address of name-dropping principal hosted by daft lord

indicators.note: N for name is dropped from the word
the host holds the guest inside
something daft is mixed up, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: DEAN, a college principal, without N

explanation.surface: A silly peer name-drops while patronising a college head.
explanation.walkthrough: Name-dropping sounds like social boasting, but it is an instruction to take N out; the daft lord then wraps around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone old dear is a patronising way to address an older woman.

clue.text: Labour's ultimate goal: food shop — really?

explanation.surface: A sceptical query about the Labour Party's final aim being a food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is political only on the surface; the labour meant is childbirth, which ends in delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: The aim of labour in childbirth is the delivery of the baby.

clue.text: Queen trashed suite, having a ball? Exactly!

indicators.note: something trashed is wrecked, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A rock star wrecks a hotel suite while partying, and someone asks whether they had a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen suggests the rock band known for trashing hotels, but gives only Q.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite so is an agreeing reply, like Exactly!

clue.text: Question by university, no trouble for Dicky

explanation.surface: A university question that gives a student called Dicky no bother.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name but is British slang for unwell or shaky, as in a dicky tummy.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling queasy means feeling dicky, slightly sick.

clue.text: Work by artist, said to be one involved with glasses

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is written as it sounds

explanation.surface: A painting's creator is rumoured to be a drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasses suggests drinking, but they are spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician tests eyes and supplies glasses.

clue.text: Role-playing welcomed by board — all right?

indicators.note: letters at play move about into a new order
one welcomed is taken inside

explanation.surface: A company board asks whether its role-play session is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: Role-playing reads as a single activity, but role is the letters and playing the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of acceptable, good enough but no more.

clue.text: A hotel in Bristol, one exotic place

indicators.note: one part goes inside another

parts.note: Bristol City is rhyming slang for titty, so a Bristol is a breast, or tit
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel in the English city of Bristol is praised as exotic.
explanation.walkthrough: Bristol is the English port city on the surface; in rhyming slang (Bristol City, titty) it means a breast.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is a South Pacific island, an exotic place.

clue.text: Buy empty container for fruit? Bloody hell!

indicators.note: an emptied word loses its insides, keeping its outer letters
the outer word holds the next one

explanation.surface: An outburst at having to buy an empty box for fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Blimey is a British exclamation of surprise, milder than bloody hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Blimey is a British exclamation of shock, like Bloody hell!

clue.text: Dark drink (cap to be removed)

indicators.note: the named part is taken away

parts.note: a nightcap is a drink before bed

explanation.surface: A dark beer whose bottle cap needs to come off.
explanation.walkthrough: Cap looks like the bottle top but is the literal letters CAP taken off the end of nightcap.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the dark part of the day; the dark is another word for night.

clue.text: (& 9ac.) Skiing but hardly getting any better?

definitions.meaning: a skier travels down the slope

explanation.surface: A beginner skier who takes to the slopes but never improves.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase is read literally for the skier and figuratively for decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Going downhill is both what skiers do and an idiom for deteriorating.

clue.text: A piece from Posh — a vocal shambles

indicators.note: the answer is a piece taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A track by Posh Spice is judged a tuneless mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Posh is Victoria Beckham, Posh Spice of the Spice Girls, whose singing was often mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns mean a scene of chaos and disorder.

clue.text: One working conman is not someone looking forward to retirement

definitions.text: not someone looking forward to retirement

indicators.note: letters at work are moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as it stands before the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A swindler with a job has no wish to stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement means going to bed, not leaving work; an insomniac dreads it.
explanation.definitionFit: An insomniac cannot sleep, so bedtime is nothing to look forward to.

clue.text: see 5dn.
Husband, knocked about and crushed

indicators.note: one part goes around another

parts.note: knocked, as in criticised, is trashed

explanation.surface: A husband has been beaten up and flattened.
explanation.walkthrough: Knocked about looks like one phrase, but about is the instruction that puts TRASHED around H.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sporting sense of beaten heavily.

clue.text: Poser's morning drink — energy's returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A show-off's morning drink is an energy drink that has come back up.
explanation.walkthrough: Poser suggests a show-off, but here it is a puzzling question.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a poser is a puzzling question.
